I fixed it: a single line of quantity 1 at 62.5¢ now totals **$0.63**, and a 62.5¢ credit comes out as -$0.63, as `README.md` says. All 13 tests pass with `make check`, including new ones that fail on the old code.

**Cause:** `to_cents` in `invoicer/money.py` used Python's `round(mills / 10)`. Python's `round` sends exact halves to the nearest even number (`round(62.5) == 62`, `round(63.5) == 64`). So any amount ending in exactly half a cent was rounded down about half the time, which is why the errors were only ever one cent.

**Fix:**
- **`invoicer/money.py`:** `to_cents` now rounds halves away from zero (62.5 → 63, -62.5 → -63) and uses exact arithmetic with no floating point. Every amount (line totals, subtotals and tax) goes through this one function, so they're all fixed together.
- **`invoicer/totals.py`:** `tax_cents` now passes an exact fraction to `to_cents` instead of a float. Tax had the same bug: for example, 100¢ at 0.5% is exactly 0.5¢, which came out as 0¢ but is now 1¢.
- **`tests/test_totals.py`:** new tests cover your 62.5¢ example, the matching credit, values just under half a cent, and the half-cent tax case.

The existing test totals didn't change. Any real invoice with an exact half cent in a subtotal or in tax will now total one cent more (or, for a credit, one cent more negative).

**Separate issue, not changed:** in `invoicer/scheduler.py`, `send_reminders` builds its list from `due_invoices(...) + overdue_invoices(...)`. Every overdue invoice is also "due", so overdue customers get two reminders. I can fix that separately if you want.
